_note: Slots for [brg_home-about-slider]. A second version of What We're About (Sean, 3 Nov): full-screen, one slide at a time (Our Vision, Our Mission), advanced by scrolling or by the arrows. Declared beside the fragment so a slot and its {token} ship in one commit. Generated into website/acf/ by `python3 kit/build-acf.py`; never hand-edit an acf.json. Slot names are underscore-only. Defaults are esc_html'd on fill, so write literal characters.

heading.label: Heading
heading.doc: The yellow marker label that sits across the top, over the photo. Leave it empty to hide the label.

slider_style.label: Style
slider_style.doc:
How one slide gives way to the next.

Photo slides across: the photo slides over to the other side, covering the words, and the next words come up on the side it left. The photo and the words swap sides on every slide.

Stays in place: nothing moves sideways. The words split up and out of the top, the photo wipes out upward, then the next photo and words come up from the bottom. The photo stays on the side chosen in Photo side.

On a phone both styles are the same: the photo on top (70% of the screen), the words underneath (30%).

photo_side.label: Photo side
photo_side.doc: Which side the photo is on for the first slide. In "Photo slides across" it moves to the other side on the next slide and back again after that; in "Stays in place" it stays here for every slide. Wide screens only: on a phone the photo is always on top.

scroll_step.label: Scrolling per slide
scroll_step.doc: How long the section holds each slide while you scroll. The first slide holds a little (so the section locks in before anything moves) and the last holds before the page carries on. Short is brisk, Medium is a calm pause, Long makes you scroll further. The arrows always move exactly one slide, and slides never change faster than about once every second and a quarter, whatever the scroll speed.

photo_px.label: Photo — movement
photo_px.doc: How far the photos drift inside their frame as you scroll through the section, as a percentage of the frame's height. 0 is off. The section stays pinned while you scroll, so the drift follows how far you are through it: the photos start at one end of their travel and finish at the other. The photo is laid out taller than its frame and slides within it, so an edge never appears and it is never zoomed. 40 is the ceiling.

photo_px_dir.label: Photo — movement direction
photo_px_dir.doc: Which way the photos travel as you scroll down through the section.

slides.label: Slides
slides.doc:
One row per slide, in order. The photo is shown with the words beside it. Landscape or portrait both work: the photo is cropped to fill its half of the screen (on a phone, the top 70%).

UNTIL YOU ADD THE FIRST ONE HERE the section shows Our Vision and Our Mission. Adding one replaces both, so add every slide you want, not only the one you are changing. Two to four slides works best.

title.label: Title
title.doc: The big words, in the brand face, for example Our Vision.

body.label: Words under the title
body.doc: One or two sentences. Write an em dash as a literal character, not as an entity.

image.label: Photo
image.doc: The photo for this slide. About 1400 x 1600 or larger; it is cropped to fill.

section_color.label: Section color
section_color.doc:
The flat color behind this whole section (the words sit straight on it, with no panel of their own, and the photo covers half of it). "As designed" leaves the light gray it has (#EDEDEE); nothing changes until you choose one.

Light, Dark, Accent and Alt accent are ROLES: what each looks like is set once on the Site-wide page, so changing Accent there repaints every section set to Accent as well as every accent button. The named shades are fixed colors. "Custom" uses the color box next to this one. The words flip to dark or light on their own so they stay readable (see Section text color).

section_color_custom.label: Section color — custom
section_color_custom.doc: Used only when Section color is set to Custom. Pick any color. Left empty, a Custom choice does nothing and the section keeps the color it has today.

section_text.label: Section text color
section_text.doc: Automatic picks dark or light words, whichever reads better on the color above. Choose Dark or Light to force it. Does nothing while Section color is "As designed".

section_color_opacity.label: Section color — opacity
section_color_opacity.doc: How solid the section color is. 100% is a flat color. Lower it to let what is behind the section show through: the page behind it, and with Section background on "color on top" the picture too. Works with any color except "As designed". The words pick dark or light for the color as if it sat on white, so on a very pale mix you may want to force Section text color.
